questions.answer: Let \(u=2x+1\). Then \(f=u^5\), so \(df/du=5u^4\), and \(du/dx=2\). By the chain rule, \(f'(x)=5(2x+1)^4\cdot2=10(2x+1)^4\).
The outside function is \(\sin u\), whose derivative is \(\cos u\). The inside function is \(u=3x\), with derivative \(3\). Therefore \(\frac{dy}{dx}=\cos(3x)\cdot3=3\cos(3x)\).
Let \(u=x^2+1\). The derivative of \(e^u\) with respect to \(u\) is \(e^u\), and \(du/dx=2x\). By the chain rule, \(f'(x)=e^{x^2+1}\cdot2x=2xe^{x^2+1}\).
Let \(u=x^2+4\). The derivative of \(\ln u\) is \(1/u\), and \(du/dx=2x\). Therefore \(f'(x)=\frac{1}{x^2+4}\cdot2x=\frac{2x}{x^2+4}\).
Let \(u=x^3-2x\). The outside function is \(u^4\), whose derivative is \(4u^3\). The inside derivative is \(du/dx=3x^2-2\). Thus \(\frac{dy}{dx}=4(x^3-2x)^3(3x^2-2)\).
Rewrite the function as \((\cos x)^2\). Let \(u=\cos x\). Then the outside derivative is \(2u\), and \(du/dx=-\sin x\). Therefore \(f'(x)=2\cos x(-\sin x)=-2\sin x\cos x\).
This is a nested composition. Let \(u=(x^2+1)^3\). Then \(d(\sin u)/dx=\cos(u)u'\). Now differentiate \(u\): \(u'=3(x^2+1)^2\cdot2x=6x(x^2+1)^2\). Therefore \(f'(x)=6x(x^2+1)^2\cos((x^2+1)^3)\).

Rewrite as \(f(x)=(1+x^2)^{-3}\). Let \(u=1+x^2\). The outside derivative is \(-3u^{-4}\), and \(du/dx=2x\). Therefore \(f'(x)=-3(1+x^2)^{-4}(2x)=-6x(1+x^2)^{-4}\). Equivalently, \(f'(x)=-\frac{6x}{(1+x^2)^4}\).
First differentiate using the chain rule. Let \(u=3x^2-1\). Then \(f'(x)=4(3x^2-1)^3\cdot6x=24x(3x^2-1)^3\). Now evaluate at \(x=1\): \(f'(1)=24(1)(3-1)^3=24\cdot8=192\).
